lens: (1) Every PMID/DOI/PMCID/accession fetched from PubMed/PMC and checked against the sentence citing it, with a retraction and expression-of-concern sweep; every block quotation checked verbatim against the version actually cited. (2) Every number and quotation traced to the script that produced it; both generators re-run with --check; every decision rule the code applies compared against what the paper discloses.
what_i_read: RE-RUN: atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py --check -> 'OK - the artifact re-derives byte-identically from the committed inputs cache' (exit 0)
PMC full text: PMC13223543 (Gracilla et al., Cancer Res 2026 - the version of record), 74,765 chars
git log -S on the three 'fixed before the numbers' cuts
central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis is not supported by its computational shadow in public data: part A finds the DepMap 'EMC' line is recorded as fusion-negative, part B grades the EMC tumour signature WEAK (GENERIC_ONLY) on two independent series, part C reports the CRISPR readout as blind, part D reports 1 of 4 pre-registered mechanism tests passing; and section 8 reports a competing HRD-based ATR programme that weakens route 1. The structural argument for the wet-lab ask is unaffected.

p1s.summary: Part D's four 'bars fixed before the numbers' are applied with numeric thresholds the paper never states, in a document whose SS1 explicitly promises 'the cuts themselves, stated so they can be checked'. Three undisclosed rules.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2907-2908: `spec[pname]['atri_specific'] = bool(a is not None and c0 is not None and abs(a) > 0.1 and abs(a) > 1.5 * abs(c0))` - the drug-specificity bar is a 0.1 MAGNITUDE FLOOR plus a 1.5x RATIO, neither stated. Line 2926: `srec['beats_the_proliferation_control'] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)` - a 15% MARGIN, while SS5's table column reads only 'vs proliferation control (rho = -0.171)' with 'beats it' / 'is larger'. Line 2965: `out['tracks_mechanism'] = bool(tests and n_pass >= 2)` - the verdict SENSITIVITY_DOES_NOT_TRACK_MECHANISM turns on a >=2-of-4 threshold the paper never prints, though it prints '1 of 4'. By contrast SS1 lists exactly three cuts (>0.2, `bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1`, < -0.5) and I confirmed all three are correctly cited to emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2309-2322 and depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py line 97, and that git log -S shows none has been edited since introduction (all three introduced in 922366a42, no later commit touches them). Numerically none of the undisclosed rules changes a verdict here (passing predictor 0.2123 clears 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.1968; the three failing expression predictors fail on a plain comparison too), so this is a disclosure defect, not a result defect.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Printing the three thresholds in SS1 alongside the three already there, and adding the >=2-of-4 rule to SS5's 'four bars' sentence. Removing or softening SS1's promise that the cuts are 'stated so they can be checked' would NOT fix it - the bars are load-bearing for SS5's verdict.

p1s.summary: The ATM row's failure of the 'vs non-DDR drugs' control - a claim repeated in the HEADLINE and in SS5 - is caused by the undisclosed |rho| > 0.1 magnitude floor, not by any correlation with the non-DDR control drugs. On the specificity comparison the paper actually shows, the ATM predictor CLEARS the bar by 2.7x.
p1s.evidence: Artifact `part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity['expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair']`: mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = -0.0903, mean_rho_across_non_DDR_controls = -0.0333, atri_specific = false. Applying line 2908: the ratio clause is 0.0903 > 1.5 x 0.0333 = 0.04995 -> TRUE; the floor clause is 0.0903 > 0.1 -> FALSE. The flag is false only because of the floor. The paper's HEADLINE says the ATM predictor 'is the one predictor that also fails the drug-specificity control' and SS5 repeats 'it is also the one predictor that fails the drug-specificity test', while SS5's table prints the column as 'vs non-DDR drugs | -0.033 X'. The column's marks are not monotone in the printed number - -0.033 gets X while +0.062 (held-out FET signature, rho -0.1379) gets a tick and +0.014 gets a tick - so no reader can reconstruct the rule from what is printed. `expr::control_oxphos` (rho -0.0564) is false for the same floor reason.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Either state the bar in full ('|rho| > 0.1 and |rho| > 1.5x the non-DDR control mean') and say the ATM row fails it on magnitude, or relabel the column so the mark is not attributed to the non-DDR comparison. Merely deleting the -0.033 number would hide the inconsistency rather than resolve it.

p1s.summary: Part B's readability filter and the series-choice rule's primary key are applied but never disclosed; the paper states the choice rule as 'more EMC samples', which is the operative tiebreak here but is not the rule.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2106-2113: `MIN_SCORED_CONCEPTS = 3` and `_platform_readable` requires `_status == 'scored'` AND >=3 EMC samples AND >=3 comparator samples AND >=3 scored concepts. Line 2142-2145: `_rank_key` sorts on `(-len(readable_platforms), -n_EMC, -max_scored_concepts_on_one_platform, ser)` - the PRIMARY key is the number of readable platforms, not the EMC count. SS3.4 says only 'Which series carries the verdict is decided by a rule fixed before the numbers, and it picked GSE4303 (more EMC samples)', and its table's 'readable?' column shows ticks and crosses with no threshold given. From the artifact, GSE4303 and GSE24369 each have readable_platforms = 1, so the tie did fall to n_EMC (10 vs 6) and the paper's account of the outcome is correct - but the filter that decided readability (3/3/3), and which moved the tier from NOT_ASSESSABLE to WEAK, is nowhere in the paper. `MIN_GROUP_N = 5` (line 335), applied to Part C's Welch tests at lines 2484/2487/2516, is likewise undisclosed.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: One sentence in SS3.4 giving the readability predicate and the full rank order. Changing the thresholds instead would move the tier and is the thing SS1 exists to forbid.

p1s.summary: The document's own headline artifact still cites only the SUPERSEDED preprint identifier for its source hypothesis - the identical one-of-a-pair defect the Appendix says was found and fixed, unfixed in the OTHER producing module.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> `_hypothesis_source`: 'FET fusion oncoproteins disrupt physiologic DNA repair and create a targetable opportunity for ATR inhibitor therapy - bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 / PMID 37205599'. `grep -o 41811428 emc-atr-vulnerability.json | wc -l` = 0; `grep -o 37205599` = 1. The source constant is emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 3122 ('10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 / PMID 37205599'), with the same in the module docstring (line 10) and at line 859. The Appendix row for this defect reads 'PMID 37205599 cited alone for route 1's mechanism paper ... the version of record is Gracilla et al., Cancer Research 2026;86:2660-2677, PMID 41811428 - already corrected in the companion document's own reference list but not propagated here until a hardening round', and a second row records the pair-defect ('the prose citation had been corrected to the published record while the producing instrument was still fetching only the preprint'). That fix was made in atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py (lines 118-119 carry MECHANISM_PMID = 41811428 and MECHANISM_PREPRINT_PMID = 37205599, and the artifact records pmid_of_record 41811428 - verified correct). It was not made in emc_atr_vulnerability.py, which produces parts A-D and the framing, and whose SS7 the paper describes as the place 'every number above' lives.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Adding the version of record to `_hypothesis_source` in emc_atr_vulnerability.py and regenerating (--check currently REPRODUCES, so the regeneration is free). Correcting only the manuscript would reproduce the exact pair-defect the Appendix documents.

p1s.summary: SS8's producer header claims '--check re-derives every statement below offline from the committed inputs cache', but SS8.2's four comparative claims about the PUBLISHED version's wording are carried by no artifact - the cache holds only the preprint. (I verified all four claims independently and every one is TRUE; this is a provenance gap, not a factual error.)
p1s.evidence: atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json: `mechanism_pmcid` = 'PMC10187251' (the preprint) and `mechanism_fulltext_xml` is the bioRxiv JATS record (journal-title 'bioRxiv', article-id pmid 37205599, 127 occurrences of 'EWSR1-FLI1', 0 of 'EWSR1::FLI1'). `grep -c 'section heading' atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json` = 0. The artifact itself says `_version_read`: 'PREPRINT' and the paper honestly says the published sentence count is UNKNOWN - but the sentences 'Throughout, ES becomes Ewing sarcoma and EWSR1-FLI1 becomes EWSR1::FLI1', 'the second quotation appears there as a section heading and a figure caption rather than a running sentence' and 'the last is split across a paragraph by the publisher' are assertions about a document the instrument never fetched. Independent check against PMC13223543 (PubMed/PMC full text of PMID 41811428, DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-2166): 130 'Ewing sarcoma', 135 'EWSR1::FLI1', 0 'EWSR1-FLI1'; 'Ewing sarcoma patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency' occurs exactly twice, once as a results section heading and once as the Figure 2 caption title; and the final preprint sentence appears split into three sentences ('We find that Ewing sarcoma tumors are not "BRCA-like" (i.e., isolated loss of HR) but rather harbor partial ATM defects. ... These data may explain the lack of clinical responses to PARP inhibitor monotherapy in patients ...'). All four claims are correct.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Either narrow the SS8 header ('--check re-derives every NUMBER below') or run the --fetch the paper already says is needed, so the published-version text is in the cache. Note the published version IS open in PMC (PMC13223543), so the fetch is a $0 CI step, not a paywall problem.

p2s.summary: One SS8.2 block quotation silently drops the source's inline reference marker, with no ellipsis or bracket.
p2s.evidence: Paper: 'Contrary to the current classification of ES as a BRCA-like tumor with defective HR, we nominate suppression of ATM activation...'. Cached preprint sentence (atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> fulltext_sentences_mentioning_HR_or_BRCA_or_PARP): 'Contrary to the current classification of ES as a BRCA-like tumor with defective HR 15 , we nominate suppression of ATM activation...'. The other four quotations are byte-verbatim against the cache apart from curly-vs-straight quote marks.

p2s.summary: The paper prints rho throughout SS5 but never says which correlation it is.
p2s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2837 calls `_spearman(...)`, whose docstring says 'Spearman rho + the Fisher-z t statistic. Rank-based, so it survives the two-colour log-ratio scale ... without either being transformed'. Nothing in SS5 identifies the statistic as Spearman, and the choice is load-bearing for the two-colour GSE4303 scale.

p2s.summary: The Bangerter citation's year disagrees with the year in the document's own committed cache.
p2s.evidence: SS2.2 cites 'Bangerter et al., Hum Cell 2022;36:446-455, PMID 36316541'. The document's own emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json -> part_a.literature.results['"H-EMC-SS"'].rows records that PMID with year '2023'. PubMed's PubDate field reads 2022 Nov 01 while the journal issue is volume 36 issue 1, pages 446-455 (a 2023 issue), so both years have a source - but the manuscript and its artifact disagree. The QUOTATION is exact: PubMed's abstract for 36316541 reads 'EMCs are translocation sarcomas and harbor in > 90% of the cases an NR4A3 rearrangement.'

p2s.summary: GSE299349's deposit date is given three different ways across the document and its artifact.
p2s.evidence: SS3.0a: 'GSE299349 ... 68 samples, deposited 2026-06-04'. SS8.1: 'submitted Jun 09 2025, released Jun 04 2026'. atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> series_record: `submission_date` 'Jun 09 2025', `last_update_date` 'Jun 04 2026' - there is no 'released' field; SS8.1 relabels last_update_date as a release date, and SS3.0a relabels it as a deposit date while the deposit was 2025.

p2s.summary: SS4's 'fraction dependent' column is a panel-wide fraction, presented inside prose that frames it as a property of the sarcoma pool.
p2s.evidence: The table's 0.992 / 1.000 / 0.726 / 0.007 values come from `part_c_coordinated_dependency.per_gene[GENE].frac_dependent_panel_wide`, i.e. over all DepMap lines. The artifact carries a separate `knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator.frac_lines_dependent_on_axis_sarcoma_pool` = 1.0. SS4's surrounding sentence reads 'the axis sits at the floor in both groups - mean -1.340 across the sarcoma pool, 99.2-100 % of lines dependent on ATR and CHEK1', which reads as if the fractions are also over the sarcoma pool. SS1 says only 'the fraction of lines with a CRISPR gene effect below -0.5' without naming the population.

_verdict_note: CLEAN, recorded because a clean sweep is worth as much as a finding. CITATIONS: all five identifiers in the manuscript fetched from PubMed and correct in every particular - 36316541 (Bangerter, Hum Cell, abstract quote verbatim, doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x), 41811428 (Gracilla DE, Menon S, ... Tulpule A, Cancer Res 2026;86:2660-2677 - author order does change from the preprint exactly as the paper says), 41651400 (Planas-Paz L, Zehnder M, Desboeufs N, Kollar S, Chen Y, Schneebeli S, Schenk R, Schmid MP, Lopes M, Weber A, Pauli C, Cancer Lett 2026;642:218300, doi 10.1016/j.canlet.2026.218300 - the eleven-name author list in SS8.1 matches exactly, and the paper is correctly described as not open access: no PMC id exists), 37205599 / PMC10187251 / doi 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 (Menon S, Gracilla D, ... bioRxiv), 34413129 (the paper Cellosaurus cites for its caution). RETRACTION/EoC SWEEP: clean. No cited item carries a retraction or expression of concern. The one expression-of-concern link in the cached preprint XML (related-article type expression-of-concern, PubMed 39637007) attaches to the preprint's REFERENCE 52 (Kolas et al., Science 2007, PMID 18006705), not to the preprint; PMID 39637007 is Thorp HH, 'Editorial Expression of Concern', Science 2024;386(6726):1102, doi 10.1126/science.adu7744, and this manuscript does not cite Kolas. METHODS CITATIONS: all four verified and none retracted - Milacic et al., 'The Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase 2024', Nucleic Acids Res 2024;52(D1):D672-D678 (PMID 37941124); Ashburner et al., 'Gene ontology: tool for the unification of biology', Nat Genet 2000;25(1):25-9 (PMID 10802651); Liberzon et al., 'The Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) hallmark gene set collection', Cell Syst 2015;1(6):417-425 (PMID 26771021); Kuleshov et al., 'Enrichr ... 2016 update', Nucleic Acids Res 2016;44(W1):W90-7 (PMID 27141961). CELLOSAURUS: api.cellosaurus.org is blocked at this sandbox's egress proxy, so the record was read from the committed cache - the caution is quoted byte-verbatim, and the '16 distinct markers - 15 STR loci plus amelogenin' count and the '18 lines including a Source(s): header and a second D13S317 allele' explanation are both exactly right against the ST block; DepMap ACH-001519, Cosmic-CLP 907290 and RCB RCB0508 are all present as stated. LITERATURE COUNT: 'of 21 Europe PMC records naming H-EMC-SS, exactly one mentions NR4A3' is exact - hit_count 21, and the single row with a non-empty mentions_nr4a3_alias is PMID 36316541, the paper establishing USZ20-EMC1/USZ22-EMC2, exactly as described. QUOTATIONS: four of the five SS8.2 block quotations are byte-verbatim in the cached preprint and the fifth differs only by the dropped reference marker (P2); the manuscript's claim that these are PREPRINT wording is correct and matches the artifact's own `_version_read`; the appendix's '156,566-byte PMC full text ... fetched 2026-08-27' is exact (len(xml.encode('utf-8')) = 156566, fetched_utc 2026-08-27T04:35:40Z). INSTRUMENTS: both generators re-run and both are current - emc_atr_vulnerability.py --check prints REPRODUCES, atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py --check prints byte-identical, so no stale artifact sits behind a fresh sentence. The version-of-record-first fetch that SS8.2 describes is really implemented (MECHANISM_PMID tried before MECHANISM_PREPRINT_PMID at lines 311 and 1234/1261, `_version_read` recorded), and 'all 54 stored' is true (n_such_sentences 54, n_such_sentences_stored 54, list length 54). The SS8.1 author-search bug is documented in the module's own source at line 269-277 and confirmed in git history; the committed query is now the fixed `AUTH:"Pauli" AND AUTH:"Planas-Paz"` with hitCount 10. NUMBERS: I re-derived every number I read in SS1, SS2, SS3.4, SS4, SS5, SS8.1 and SS8.3 from the two artifacts and every one matched, including the values a previous round corrected - GSE24369 20,629 probes / 0.982, ATM -0.0041 pooled and -0.0005 on the FET arm, MYC t 3.342, oxphos t 5.918, checkpoint-FET +0.1034 / t 1.735; GPL3290 27,196 / 0.582; DNA Repair +0.1778 (t 3.329) vs adipogenesis +0.2183 (t 5.081); ATR -1.3859 / -1.4452 / SD 0.2685 / 0.992 / t 1.231; axis mean -1.340, SD 0.1904, delta -0.0065 (the SD is `axis_sd_sarcoma_pool`, correctly paired, not ATM's coincidentally similar 0.1901); joint z -0.0475 vs +0.0134, t -0.41, 1/20 vs 3/71; every per-drug rho, t and n in the seven-drug table; 956 and 892 lines; the 2.7-7.1x per-drug disagreement (2.72, 5.81, 7.07); rho SE 1/sqrt(700-3) = 0.0379; NR4A3 13.332 TPM rank 4, family fraction 0.0634 rank 29, median 0.0524, NR4A1 196.784 (14.8x), row range 162,218-188,597. All twelve gene sets match SS3.2's table by name, size and library. GENERATOR STABILITY: git log -S confirms none of the three cuts named in SS1 has been edited since it was introduced, so 'fixed before the numbers' is verifiable as claimed. VERDICT: no blocker. The five P1s are all disclosure or provenance defects - an undisclosed threshold, a mark whose cause is misattributed, a filter that is applied but not printed, an artifact still naming a superseded identifier, and a set of true claims about a source the instrument never fetched. None of them moves a number, a tier or a verdict, and the paper's negatives are reported at their true weight throughout.
